title: Infinite magic and the emergence of the continuum
authors: Leo Shaposhnik, Lorenzo Leone, Lennart Bittel, Dimitris Saraidaris, Alexander Jahn, Jens Eisert
abstract: Which features of a quantum state are needed for a relativistic quantum field theory to emerge from a lattice system? We address this question by establishing a quantitative relationship between the type classification of hyperfinite von Neumann algebras and the quantum-information-theoretic resource of nonstabilizerness, also called magic. Our results establish two complementary parts of this relationship. First, we prove that any stabilizer system on a lattice defines a canonical GNS Hilbert space in which local von Neumann algebras do not contain type III factors in their central decomposition. As an explicit example, we prove that for stabilizer systems with short-range order, the local algebras are isomorphic to tensor products of hyperfinite factors of type I or type II. This demonstrates that the absence of magic is accompanied by the absence of type III factors in the local algebras, therefore prohibiting the appearance of a quantum field theory. Second, for the hyperfinite factors of Araki, Woods and Powers, we prove a quantitative equivalence: The limiting factor is of type III if and only if the locally optimized min-relative entropy of magic diverges. This divergence is necessary to generate the continuous spectrum associated to a type III factor. Thus, in this setting, the emergence of a type III factor requires not merely the presence of magic, but an infinite amount of it. These results provide a rigorous setting supporting the proposal that infinite magic is a necessary structural ingredient for the emergence of a relativistic continuum from lattice systems.
summary: This work connects the emergence of relativistic Quantum Field Theories from lattice models to the quantum information resource known as 'magic.' It proves that while simple stabilizer systems cannot support QFT, the appearance of the necessary type III factor requires an infinite amount of 'magic' in the underlying quantum state structure.
main_problem: The paper seeks to establish the necessary quantum-information-theoretic conditions for a relativistic Quantum Field Theory (QFT) to emerge from a discrete lattice system.
main_result: The emergence of a type III factor, characteristic of QFT, requires the presence of 'infinite magic' (divergence of the min-relative entropy of magic) when starting from hyperfinite lattice algebras.
method: The authors use advanced techniques from operator algebras (Von Neumann algebras), quantum information theory (nonstabilizerness/magic), and the study of infinite tensor products.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on local algebras derived from stabilizer systems on a lattice, which serve as a model for quantum states on a discrete spacetime structure.
key_observables: The type of the local von Neumann algebra (Type I, II, or III factor) and the quantum information resource called 'magic' (quantified by min-relative entropy).
important_parameters: The divergence of the locally optimized min-relative entropy of magic, which signals the transition to a type III factor.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing quantitative equivalences between algebraic structure (Type III) and information-theoretic properties (infinite magic) in specific mathematical settings.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes reference mathematical equations defining structures like local algebras and entropy calculations.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first analyzing the constraints imposed by stabilizer systems (showing they preclude type III factors) and then tackling the general case using hyperfinite factors, establishing the necessary and sufficient condition linking type III structure to the divergence of magic.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, information-theoretic criterion for the emergence of continuous spacetime structures (QFT) from discrete quantum systems, linking fundamental concepts in quantum information to high-energy physics.
